properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Asylum Twp, Bradford County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/01/2022 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Asylum Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/11/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 966807
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 9/01/2022
Comments: On 9/21/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. It was 67 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived on site I met Tim Artman who is overseeing the coil tubing operations and Robert Rueckert who is overseeing the work-over-rig operations.Halliburton finished fracking nine wells on Saturday 8/27/2022 and rigged out on Sunday 8/28/2022. There was a site handoff on 8/29/2022 and the coil tubing and workover rig moved in after that. The two crews are conducting post frac cleanout/drillout operations. The crews were working on the first two wells, the 4HC and 22HC. Tim expects it to take about a week to complete the nine wells.Tim and Robert accompanied me on the inspection. I field tested numerous water/mud puddles around the location with the following results: 4'x20' water puddle near the entrance of the site by two residual waste containers measured 4.12 mS conductance.20'x30' water/mud puddle by brine tanks on south side of pad field tested at 3.79 mS conductance. The brine tanks are left over from fracking operations and not being used by the current operations being conducted on site.I field tested a small 1'x2' puddle of water in the area identified in previous inspections as having high conductance with the current result being 9.33 mS conductance.20'x40' water/mud puddle east of the high conductance area and outside of the secondary containment field tested at 8.61 mS conductance.30'x40' puddle on north edge of pad field tested at 2.32 mS conductance.2'x2' water puddle at the bottom of rock area on east fill slope measured 4.22 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-025 from this area for laboratory analysis. I contacted Eric Hottenstein concerning the continued high conductance of water/mud on the pad surface and about the elevated conductance water puddle found on the fill slope. He is mobilizing someone to assess the water puddle on the fill slope and reported the following: Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to inspection 3409693 conducted on 8/11/2022. Chesapeake will begin assessment and cleanup operations when current work activities are concluded and the rig matting and secondary containment plastic has been removed.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration berms. Infiltration berm 2 is not adequately stabilized.The DEP recommends the following:1. Assess the area noted with high conductance water on the fill slope and provide immediate protection as necessary to prevent pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.2. Continue to remove fluids from the high-conductance areas noted in this and previous inspections.3. Continue to monitor the stabilization of infiltration area 2 and provide additional resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 10:30 hrs.

Permit API: 065-25518
Unconventional: No

Comments: This site located west off Odonnell Road, 1 1/2 miles south of railroad crossing on State Game Lands Road, at the end of second branch to the north. Well is set-up for production with a meter, separator and one tank. A report of a release of 32 gallons of produced water was reported by Will Warfel with Diversified Prod LLC at 12:30 on 9/21/23 at this well site. The release was assumed to be from the separator, there is an area of no vegetation around the well head, separator and meter and a path 70x15' path to the west. Contaminated soil needs to be removed from site and hauled to a licensed disposal facility. This follow-up inspection by WQS Taylor showed no additional clean-up activity has been completed at this site. The previous inspection detailed increased conductivity levels in areas around the well head, separator and in an area of dead vegetation west of the well set-up. Conductivity tested in vegetated area west of well head read 106 micro siemansClean-up of this site is not completed and will require Act 2 SOP to remediate this site.

properties.content:

Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8177497
Permit API: 053-31042
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/28/2024
Comments: This follow up inspection was conducted to evaluate the open violations at this site which were issued on November 21, 2023. The access road and site location have not been stoned. The culverts, ditches, and sumps at this location have been installed. The areas of earth disturbance along the banks of the site and access road have been mulched, however, several areas are not sufficient due to washing away over time. These areas will require added temporary stabilization. Upon arriving at the site at approximately 13:15, there was no precipitation occurring. At approximately 13:30, it began to lightly rain. It was noted that the access roads leading to the proposed wells upslope of the Hastings SDT 47 proposed well site showed evidence of accelerated erosion (see Photos 1 and 2). Due to the up slope road surface not having stone, that the up slope ditches, culverts, and sumps became overwhelmed with sediment laden water (see Photo 3). The culvert at the Hastings SDT 47 site location was receiving a large volume of sediment laden water from the up slope roads (see Photo 4). This sediment laden water was traveling through the woods and directly discharging into Hastings Run (see Photos 5 and 6). Down stream of the discharge, the sediment laden water is clearly pictured from bank to bank (see Photo 7). This photo was taken after the rain had stopped at approximately 14:00. The rain was varying in intensity over the course of the 30 minutes with approximately 10 minutes of heavy down fall. A voicemail was left with the operator, Steven Tachoir, to discuss the results from this inspection. It was recommend to stone the access roads and site location as quickly as possible as weather permits. The issued violations noted from November 21, 2023 will be noted as outstanding as a result of this inspection.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up inspection (FUI) of the Seneca Resources - Cruttenden 846 Well Site located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 5/9/23 @1315 hours. The weather was 67 degrees, sunny, winds N @10mph. Flowback personnel from Danos and Cameron observed onsite. Temporary containment was observed installed around the 26H and 1V wells onsite. Fluid was observed in the temporary containment. Three upright production tanks were observed within secondary containment near the entrance. Puddles observed on the pad surface in front of the production tanks had field measured conductivities of 2.9 - 3.61mS/cm. A puddle was observed in the drive lane east of the producing wells with a field measured conductivity of 2.76mS/cm. The 30HU - 34HU, 39HU and 78H wells were observed in production/flowback within secondary containment. Two additional wells drilled by the previous operator, the 22H and 24H wells were also observed capable of production. Permit API: 125-27157
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/14/2025
Comments: On May 14, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Fred Jones well site in Independence Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination request was approved for this site on January 5, 2017. Dylan Stanley, Expand Energy Lease Operator, was onsite during this inspection. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the eastern cutslope of the well pad, which was reported to the DEP by the Expand Energy representative Jared Shockey on May 7, 2025. The DEP spoke Mr. Shockey on May 12, 2025, who stated that Expand Energy recently acquired this site and discovered the reported slough on the eastern cutslope upon assessing the site after acquisition. The slough is reportedly 1.5 feet deep and 100 feet long by 40 feet wide. The operator proposes to remove the sloughed material and add R4 riprap in its place as permanent stabilization.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). However, it appears to be heavily deteriorated with cracks forming in its reflective layer. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan are onsite. However, they are severely waterlogged and could not be evaluated during this inspection (see photo 2). GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a (see photo 16). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 17). Some rainwater was observed in the secondary containment of the production tanks (see photo 18). Well 206H appears to be equipped for production with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it observed (see photo 19). The faded well tag is completely illegible (see photo 20). There are two additional well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photos 21-24). The DEP spoke with Mr. Stanley onsite who stated that an order has already been placed for replacement well tags. The DEP recommended that the secondary containment of the production tanks is kept empty so it can function property in the event of a release. The DEP also recommended replacing the Act 9 sign and ERP onsite to ensure continued compliance post acquisition of site.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed (see photo 3). The slough that was reported by the operator on 5/07/2025 is present on the eastern cutslope of well pad. Its size appears to fit the dimensions reported by the operator. It does not appear to pose a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth at the time of inspection. A toe bulge was observed below the slough and possible additional cracking was observed at the southern end of the slough (see photos 5-15).Based on observations from this inspection, the DEP recommends that the operator install a new Act 9 sign, well tags, ERP, and PPC plan that are updated with the information of the current operator and comply with current regulations. The DEP also recommends that the operator monitor the slough on the eastern cutslope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on exposed soil.Violations shall be issued against the slough on the eastern cutslope of the well pad.The following information is requested from the operator:- What is being done in the interim (temporary stabilization)- What is being done in the future (permanent stabilization)If a Geotechnical Report would be necessary and/or developed for the soil crack and/or slough, please submit to DEP Technical Services. The Department recommends that the Operator coordinate with DEP Technical Services for any potential modifications to the approved ESCGP plans that may be necessary for addressing the soil crack and/or slough.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a FUI inspection at the Tilden Marcellus LLC - Simonetti 801 located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 10/2/2019 @0845 hours. The weather was sunny 74 degrees. Onsite for the inspection was myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Jennifer Compton and Nathan Smelser, Tilden Marcellus; Farm Boy Excavation; Civil and Environmental Consultants, Inc. As of today's inspection, a large stain was observed on the gravel surface adjacent to the failed dump line measuring ~8'x4'(See Photo#1). Tilden's earthmoving contractor, Farm Boy, had used a small excavator to scrape the surface of the impacted pad area, fill slope (see photo #2) and dig a sump in the fill slope approximately 4' wide and 5' deep. Fluid that had accumulated in the bottom of the sump had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm(See Photo#3). Sample 4427-192 was collected from the fluid in the fill slope sump and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for SAC 942 analysis. CEC consultants had delineated the extent of the impacted area with white flags. The excavator, and CEC, were currently working to remove soil with an elevated conductivity in an area below the toe of the fill slope(See Photo#4,5). The excavated sump was then expanded across the fill slope. A wet gravel layer was observed ~3' below the pad surface that appeared to be the source of the >19.99mS/cm fluid entering the sump(See Photo#6). Jennifer Compton and CEC continued to screen the fill slope area and remove additional material. The impacted material was being staged on the pad surface, on the interior of the gas line, awaiting the delivery of more disposal boxes. Ms. Compton was also awaiting the delivery of a super sucker truck to remove additional pad material. Tilden Marcellus and CEC were advised to contact the DEP Environment Cleanups and Brownfields (ECB) Program to facilitate cleanup activities going forward. Violations cited previously in inspection report#2939891, dated 9/30/2019 are cited as OUTSTANDING against the 2H well, API#117-20309 at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 345263

Inspection Date: 2019-10-02
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a FUI inspection at the Tilden Marcellus LLC - Simonetti 801 located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 10/2/2019 @0845 hours. The weather was sunny 74 degrees. Onsite for the inspection was myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Jennifer Compton and Nathan Smelser, Tilden Marcellus; Farm Boy Excavation; Civil and Environmental Consultants, Inc. As of today's inspection, a large stain was observed on the gravel surface adjacent to the failed dump line measuring ~8'x4'(See Photo#1). Tilden's earthmoving contractor, Farm Boy, had used a small excavator to scrape the surface of the impacted pad area, fill slope (see photo #2) and dig a sump in the fill slope approximately 4' wide and 5' deep. Fluid that had accumulated in the bottom of the sump had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm(See Photo#3). Sample 4427-192 was collected from the fluid in the fill slope sump and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for SAC 942 analysis. CEC consultants had delineated the extent of the impacted area with white flags. The excavator, and CEC, were currently working to remove soil with an elevated conductivity in an area below the toe of the fill slope(See Photo#4,5). The excavated sump was then expanded across the fill slope. A wet gravel layer was observed ~3' below the pad surface that appeared to be the source of the >19.99mS/cm fluid entering the sump(See Photo#6). Jennifer Compton and CEC continued to screen the fill slope area and remove additional material. The impacted material was being staged on the pad surface, on the interior of the gas line, awaiting the delivery of more disposal boxes. Ms. Compton was also awaiting the delivery of a super sucker truck to remove additional pad material. Tilden Marcellus and CEC were advised to contact the DEP Environment Cleanups and Brownfields (ECB) Program to facilitate cleanup activities going forward. Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-20
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil appears to be completed. Soil removal has been extended several hundred feet north of the area originally flagged as showing oil contamination from the release. Four piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. A temporary road has been stoned to access the area and for the eventual removal of the contaminated soil. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/03/2025
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 8227908
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 2/21/2024
Violation Code: 78.121(B) - WELL REPORTING – PRODUCTION REPORTING – Operator failed to electronically submit production and status report to the Department through its web site.
Violation ID: 8176352
Permit API: 065-25991
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Henderson Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/21/2024
Comments: This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Cider Mill Road in December 2007.On 10/24/22, an NOV was issued to Stonehaven Energy when it was discovered that the brine tank had been allowed to overflow. On 3/27/23, an administrative order was issued due to a lack of remedial action from Stonehaven Energy. This order was delivered in person by Bureau of Investigations staff on 3/28/2023. As per this administrative order, a written remediation plan was to be submitted to the Department by 5/26/23, and a final remediation report is to be submitted by 12/31/23. No remediation plans have been received by the Department as of this date. A Petition to Enforce was filed in Commonwealth Court on 8/16/2023. In response to that petition, a Commonwealth Order was issued on 12/13/2023 requiring a Remediation Schedule to be submitted to the Department within 60 days. No Remediation Schedule has been received, and a new violation has been issued for failure to comply with the terms of the issued court order.During an inspection of the site on 4/20/23, it was noted that a partial soil excavation had occurred. At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any further excavation has occurred since that date. The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The well valves were closed at the time of inspection, and the 50 bbl brine tank appears to be empty. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 12/7/2023 (Inspection Record # 3655977), there have been no changes at the site. New violations have been issued during this inspection for failure to comply with an issued court order, failure to plug the well upon abandonment, and for failure to submit annual production information.

Comments: The Department of Environmental (DEP) conducted a Follow-up Inspection of the Tilden Marcellus - Thomas 808 well pad located in Elk Twp, Tioga Co. on 6/12/2019 @1000 hours. The weather was rain 62 degrees. Present onsite for the inspection was Ross McMann, DEP Geologic Specialist and myself. Activity onsite consisted of Tilden Marcellus conducting stimulation activities on the 4H well. The DEP was onsite to follow-up on remediation activities associated with the 6/3/2019 release of an estimate 10 barrels of stimulation fluid outside containment. As of today's inspection, a lined ditch was observed installed across the ESE fill slope of the well pad. The ditch was collecting potentially impacted runoff from the well pad. Fluid in the ditch had a field measured conductivity of 460uS/cm. The E&S control at the base of the SE fill slope was observed full of fluid with a field measured conductivity of 420uS/cm. A pump was positioned, on containment, just upslope of the E&S control to remove water as needed. Onsite personnel stated no elevated conductivity fluid has been observed in the E&S control. Fluid along the ESE edge of the well pad had a field measured conductivity of 10.45mS/cm indicating the continued presence of a pollutional substance. Soils just off the edge of the well pad had elevated conductivity of >2.0mS/cm in the upper inch of soil. Onsite personnel stated once stimulation activities were complete, Tilden would initiate removal of the containment/rig mats, screening of the E/SE section of the pad (and surrounding areas), and removal of all impacted material. Onsite personnel were notified of any deficiencies. Violations, cited 6/4/2019 in IR#2889847, remain OUTSTANDING against the 3H well, API#117-20476. No other violations are noted at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours.

Comments: On 08/25/2025, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the plugged Hansen Engineering Inc 1 Well Site. The well was plugged on 12/12/2019. I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Jena Bonasorte (PA DEP).The following was observed:The well appeared to be plugged. A monument with the well's permit number was on location (Photos 1, 2). It appears that casing from the well may be present (Photo 3).The well site around the plugged well was not restored to original contour. Overall, the site was vegetated, however it appears that third party disturbance has occurred around the plugged well and on/adjacent to the restored access road (Photos 4-7).A culvert crossing the access road remains as well as what appears to be a roadside channel (Photos 8, 9).Electrical equipment remains (Photo 10).The Department has not received a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) from the operator following plugging and site restoration. I recommend that the WSRR is submitted. Due to the operator failing to submit a WSRR within 60 days after restoration of the well site and failure to restore the site to original conditions, violations of 78.65(3) and OGA3216(A) are being issued.
